key_insight: Function-Structured Graph RL trains a math-reasoning policy with executable code and multiple verifiers, so reward comes from both correct answers and correct intermediate structure.
engineering_relevance: The method suggests a practical way to improve LLM-based math solvers by combining structured decomposition, code execution, and verifier-guided reinforcement learning.
method: SFT trains the model to generate Python code from function-structured subproblem graphs.
GRPO then optimizes with answer-gated rewards and span-level credit assignment.
Teacher supervision and structured memory can be added for continued RL improvements.
evidence_signal: On a benchmark built from GSM8K, MathQA, MATH, and Omni-MATH, GRPO raised final-answer accuracy from 43.25% to 67.50% and full solution success from 32.25% to 52.25% over SFT.
watch_item: Verifier-based gains may depend on the quality of private specifications and careful implementation of reward gating, so execution correctness alone should not be treated as mathematical correctness.
paper_title: Function-Structured Reinforcement Learning with Executable Verifiers for Mathematical Reasoning
